title: Code coverage
recap: Statement coverage asks whether a statement ran; branch coverage asks whether every decision outcome ran. Testing one ordinary order cannot establish behavior for invalid, express, or boundary orders.
Even full branch coverage does not prove correctness: a wrong threshold may execute every branch. Boundary tests just below, at, and just above a threshold help catch those errors.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement shippingFee(weight, express). Weight <= 0 is invalid and returns -1, even for express. Valid weights 1..5 cost 5, weights 6..20 cost 10, and larger weights cost 20. Express adds 7 only to valid orders. Test both express choices in every weight category and directly on the 5/6 and 20/21 boundaries.
hints: Return the invalid result before adding express fees.
Choose a base fee from the three valid weight brackets.
Test both sides of each threshold, not just one value per branch.
